subject: VPC demarcation + traffic-shaping playbook for private deployment (draft)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme.com>; EdgeInfra Consulting <infra@edgeconsult.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: VPC demarcation + traffic-shaping playbook for private deployment (draft)

Hi Lisa / EdgeInfra team,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Monday. Attached is a first-pass playbook and a draft reference diagram that captures our proposed demarcation: control-plane peering (TLS mutual-auth), tenant data plane on private subnets, and a dedicated egress path through Acme NAT gateways.

Key points I want to surface up front:
- Control plane (Redwood CP) will peer over a dedicated peering/VPN with port restrictions to 443 and a management CIDR.
- Data plane nodes (in-customer VPC) will host inference workers; outbound tokenized telemetry and billing logs go over an egress path with a small set of allowed FQDNs.
- We propose traffic shaping on the egress gateway to cap burst rates per-tenant during warm-up, to avoid noisy-neighbor saturation.

Ask: can your network team confirm the NAT throughput and whether there is any hourly throttling in the current region? Also tagging: we included a simulated shaping policy in the attached PDF (egress-shaping-sim.pdf) and one SVG reference diagram (vpc-draft-diagram.svg).

Proposed next step: a controlled dry-run (non-prod) where we validate prefix routing + iptable shaping rules during a simulated burst. Suggested dates below.

Schedule options: 2027-04-27 (PST) or 2027-04-29 (PST). Let me know which works and who from your side should be present.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-draft-diagram.svg (image/svg+xml), egress-shaping-sim.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@edgeconsult.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC demarcation + traffic-shaping playbook for private deployment (draft)

Thanks Hannah — quick read-through notes: good direction. A few immediate constraints from our side:

- Our current NAT gateway in us-west-2 has a burst cap of ~3 Gbps for the account. Sustained egress above that will be throttled by our infra provider.
- We have a maintenance blackout 02:00-06:00 UTC Tue/Wed where routing changes are restricted.
- For compliance we need egress IPs to be documented and immutable for a 30-day window during the pilot.

Couple of asks: can you include a plan for a simulated failover to a secondary egress IP and a step that proves the KV cache persists across failover? Also please confirm whether control-plane peering supports certificate rotation without service disruption.

I attached our network constraints doc for reference.

Cheers,
Lisa Huang
Network PM, Acme Corp
lisa.huang@acme.com

Attachments: acme-network-constraints.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC demarcation + traffic-shaping playbook for private deployment (draft)

Lisa — appreciate the constraints. Quick responses inline and an updated short checklist below.

- NAT throughput: noted 3 Gbps burst cap. We will add per-tenant shaping to keep bursts < 750 Mbps per tenant (configurable) and implement graceful queueing to avoid packet drops for control traffic.
- Maintenance blackout: we will not schedule routing changes inside the blackout window. Dry-run proposed for 2027-04-29 18:00 UTC to keep outside your blackout.
- Immutable egress IPs: we will pin egress via a small set of Elastic IPs and provide a 30-day manifest for the pilot.
- CV rotation: our control-plane peering supports cert rotation via a staged rollover; we will run the rollover in canary mode and fallback to the previous cert if health checks fail — no KV cache loss expected because data plane uses local disk + replicated object store.

Updated short checklist (for the dry-run):
1) Provision two Elastic IPs and announce to Acme (Hannah / Acme Net)
2) Deploy shaping policy on egress gateway: token-bucket per-tenant, burst window 10s, sustained cap to be negotiated
3) Simulated burst: replay synthetic load (we will provide load generator) for 60s at 1.2x expected peak
4) Failover test: detach primary EIP, attach secondary, confirm TCP connections drain and reconnect; verify KV access across nodes
5) Post-test telemetry: collect packet counters, ingress/egress counters, queue drop rates, and per-tenant latency P50/P95

I’ve pushed a working copy of the playbook into the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f_vpc-playbook (read-only for Acme). Can the Acme infra team confirm EIP provisioning and whether they want us to run the synthetic load from inside their VPC or across the peering link?

If that looks good I’ll schedule the dry-run for 2027-04-29 18:00 UTC and send a calendar invite.

-Hannah

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: VPC demarcation + traffic-shaping playbook for private deployment (draft)

Hannah / team — a few technical nitpicks and a short ops snippet to include in the playbook:

1) Control-plane peering: prefer TLS mutual-auth with mTLS certs rotated via an ACME-like pipeline. Add health-check probe on /healthz that verifies control-plane leader and KV store quorum before cert swap.
2) Egress shaping: we should implement the token-bucket at the egress proxy (Envoy) layer to avoid iptables complexity on customer hosts. Envoy filter -> rate limit -> local queued-shed policy.
3) KV persistence: we use a three-node raft with a separate disk; we should include a post-failover check that runs: curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:7001/kv/status and validate raft state==leader OR followers==2.

Ops snippet to add into runbook (for dry-run):
```
# validate egress queueing stats
curl -sS http://egress-proxy.local:9901/stats | grep queue_depth
# run KV health check
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:7001/kv/status | jq '.raft.state'
# initiate cert rollover (canary)
redwoodctl cert rotate --peer acme-peering --canary
```

I also suggest we add a rollback step after every routing change: re-attach previous EIP, wait 30s, validate no client-facing error spikes.

-Jonas

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC demarcation + traffic-shaping playbook for private deployment (draft)

Perfect — thanks Jonas and Lisa.

Dry-run confirmed: 2027-04-29 18:00 UTC. Calendar invite coming; Hannah (Redwood) will own the synthetic load and initial shaping config. Acme to provision 2 EIPs and confirm a point-of-contact for real-time troubleshooting. EdgeInfra will monitor BGP/NAT counters and collect pcap if necessary.

Mutual action plan:
- Acme: provision EIPs and confirm NAT throughput by 2027-04-26 (owner: Lisa)
- Redwood: prepare shaping policy and load generator; push playbook to shared drive by 2027-04-24 (owner: Hannah)
- Jonas: add the ops snippets and rollback steps to playbook by 2027-04-24 (owner: Jonas)
- Post-test report: Redwood to produce a short RTP (results + recommendations) by 2027-05-03

Closing loop: I’ll add the snippets Jonas provided and update the diagram with an explicit EIP manifest and the staged cert rollover steps. If there are no objections I’ll mark the playbook as v0.2 after the edits.

Thanks all — looking forward to the dry-run.

Hannah
